Article Title: Day after PK's poll win, PM Modi talks to Nabin, meets Nitish
Article Text: NEW DELHI: At an NDA parliamentary party meeting on Tuesday, govt representatives emphasised the big boost to employment generation and economic growth under PM Narendra Modi's leadership compared to the preceding UPA era, with India's "transformative journey" in sports also being highlighted.Modi and home minister Amit Shah were among those who attended the meeting, though the Prime Minister did not speak at the weekly gathering of governing alliance MPs.A light-hearted conversation between Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin during the closed-door meeting sparked talk in NDA circles, as many MPs interpreted it as the PM putting the Rajya Sabha member from Bihar at ease a day after BJP suffered a shock defeat in his pocket borough of Bankipur, which he had vacated after his election to Parliament.Modi later also met former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar , who was accompanied by his JDU colleagues Lalan Singh and Sanjay Jha, in his office. TNN
Article Summary: Modi and home minister Amit Shah were among those who attended the meeting. A light-hearted conversation between Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin during the closed-door meeting sparked talk in NDA circles. Many MPs interpreted it as the PM putting the Rajya Sabha member from Bihar at ease.

Article Title: BJP attacks Cong 'double standards' on students stirs
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP accused Congress and its allies of double standards on the issue of examination irregularities as it slammed them for their alleged silence over student protests in Jharkhand and Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge's controversial comments to defend police action against protests linked to an exam.While Congress maintains silence on exam irregularities in states where it is in office, it along with its allies are not allowing Parliament to function over similar incidents, BJP said, in a reference to opposition's strident protest over NEET paper leak and related issues and its attack on home minister Amit Shah over Delhi police action against protesters on July 20."No Congress MP is seen holding a placard on Jharkhand Public Service Commission examination paper leak issue. Article Title: Vaishno Devi fake silver row: Court seeks detailed probe report, orders evidence preservation
Article Text:
The Jammu Chief Judicial Magistrate has taken decisive action by ordering the preservation of evidence in a troubling case of fake silver offerings amounting to Rs 550 crore. In response to a petition seeking to secure all relevant physical and electronic evidence, the court acknowledged allegations of adulteration and pilferage concerning around twenty tonnes of silver.

JAMMU: Jammu Chief Judicial Magistrate Munish Kumar Manhas, while hearing the case of alleged Rs 550 crore fake silver offerings at Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Ji shrine last week, directed Deputy SP Bhawan, Katra, to submit a detailed inquiry report and ordered the preservation of evidence on the next date of hearing.The CJM’s orders came on July 29 following a petition filed by advocate Deepak Sharma seeking urgent preservation of all physical, documentary, and electronic evidence linked to the controversy alleging adulteration, substitution, pilferage and suspected misappropriation of approximately 20 tonnes of silver offerings devotees had made to the shrine.The petitioner also sought safeguarding of the remaining silver or purported silver articles, samples, remnants, and residues, along with stock and vault records, weighing and dispatch registers, assay and laboratory reports, govt mint records, transportation documents and the complete chain-of-custody record. He sought protection of CCTV footage, electronic inventory data, official emails, server logs, access records, audit trails, accounting records, reconciliation statements and other digital evidence linked to the alleged scam.On May 9, Sharma submitted a complaint to IGP (crime branch) Jammu and SSP (crime branch, EOW) Jammu. The crime branch received the complaint on May 11 and forwarded it to its HQ on May 20 for further action. Crime branch HQ approved its reference to Zonal Police HQ on June 9, following which it was sent to IGP (Jammu) on June 13.The SSP said the case was currently in the inquiry stage, and no FIR had been registered yet.The CJM posted the next hearing on Aug 18.
Article Summary: Jammu Chief Judicial Magistrate orders preservation of evidence in case of fake silver offerings amounting to Rs 550 crore. The court acknowledged allegations of adulteration and pilferage concerning around twenty tonnes of silver. The CJM’s orders came on July 29 following a petition filed by advocate Deepak Sharma.

Article Title: 'Good precedent': Kangana Ranaut backs police action against Udhayanidhi Stalin for crass remark
Article Text:
Kangana Ranaut on Udhayanidhi Stalin's arrest

Kangana Ranaut post

NEW DELHI: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Tuesday backed the police action against Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , saying that although the DMK leader is now out on bail, his arrested had set a "good precedent."“Public display of filthy abuses, double-meaning obscene and vulgar jokes is not acceptable in any civilised society. Mr Stalin was sent to jail for the offence. He might be out on bail by now, but it’s a good precedent,” Ranaut, who often makes headlines for her own controversial remarks, said in a post on her Instagram Stories.Her remarks came after the Tamil Nadu Police arrested Udhayanidhi Stalin over an alleged “distasteful double-meaning remark” made during a protest on Monday against the state’s C Joseph Vijay-led government. The remark was allegedly made in response to members of the public chanting an actress’s name at a gathering in Thanjavur.The Madras high court subsequently directed the police to release the former deputy chief minister after the Tamil Nadu government informed the court that Udhayanidhi would be granted station bail following the inquiry.The submission was made during the hearing of the DMK leader’s anticipatory bail plea.During his speech on Monday, Udhayanidhi had accused chief minister C Joseph Vijay of showing little interest in resolving the Cauvery water dispute with neighbouring Karnataka or safeguarding farmers’ interests.At one point, a section of DMK supporters began chanting the name of a Tamil actress, apparently suggesting that Vijay’s priorities lay elsewhere.Udhayanidhi then paused, smiled and remarked, “The water should come there, irrespective of where it is supposed to come from.”As the crowd erupted in cheers and laughter, he added, “No. I was referring only to the Cauvery,” drawing another round of applause and laughter.

Article Title: Educationist, former Governor D Y Patil passes away at 91 in Kolhapur
Article Text:
D Y Patil, a former Governor and renowned educationist, has passed away.





KOLHAPUR: Padma Shri awardee, former Bihar, Tripura and West Bengal Governor, and renowned educationist D Y Patil, fondly known as "Dada", died at his residence in Kasba Bawda in Kolhapur on Tuesday morning following a prolonged illness. He was 91.Patil, a former Congress leader, is survived by his sons, Congress MLC Satej Patil, Sanjay Patil and Ajinkya Patil, and daughter Nandita Palshetkar.Announcing the demise of her grandfather, Smita Jadhav, Pro-Vice Chancellor of D Y Patil Pimpri, said, "It is with profound grief and a heavy heart that I inform you of the sad demise of our beloved Founder, Hon'ble Dr D Y Patil Sir. His visionary leadership, unwavering commitment to education, and extraordinary legacy have shaped countless lives and institutions. His passing is an irreparable loss to the entire D Y Patil family. "Patil was conferred the Padma Shri in 1991 for his contribution to the social sector.He was survived by son's Congress MLC Satej Patil, Sanjay Patil, Vijay Patil, Ajinkya Patil and daughters Bhageshree Patil, Supriya Patil, Rajashree Patil, Nandita Palshetkar and Pooja Patil.
Article Summary: Patil, a former Congress leader, is survived by his sons, Congress MLC Satej Patil, Sanjay Patil and Ajinkya Patil. Patil was conferred the Padma Shri in 1991 for his contribution to the social sector.

Article Title: 'Goonga Gudda': Sanjay Raut hits Amit Shah, PM Modi over silence on Jantar Mantar police action
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut labeled Union minister Amit Shah and PM Narendra Modi as 'Goonga Gudda' regarding their silence on July 20 Jantar Mantar protest





NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Wednesday took a jibe at Union home minister Amit Shah and Prime Minister Narendra Modi , calling them "Goonga Gudda (deaf doll)" for remaining silent on the July 20 police action against protesting students at Jantar Mantar.Raut was responding to questions on the ongoing political controversy over the "Goongi Gudiya" remarks made by Maharashtra Congress against deputy chief minister and Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) chief Sunetra Pawar."Their party (NCP) should answer the questions. However, their party is of Amit Shah. I ask Amit Shah, 'who gave orders for lathicharge, use of pellet guns at Jantar Mantar?' But he is mum. This means he is 'Goonga Gudda'. (PM) Modi is also 'Goonga Gudda'," Raut said while addressing a press conference here.Raut said Sunetra Pawar remained silent during a press conference when asked about the "deteriorating" law and order situation in Beed district.He said the comments made by Maharashtra Congress against Sunetra Pawar were not personal, but concerned her accountability as the state's deputy chief minister."The 'Goongi Gudiya' comment regarding Sunetra Pawar... Prithviraj Chavan has talked about it.A question was asked regarding governance and law and order situation in Beed. However, she remained quiet on it. Congress' comment was on this (issue). She is the state's deputy chief minister. She should have answered the question. However, Dhananjay Munde took the microphone near her," the UBT Sena MP said.He said that if there had been a man instead of Sunetra Pawar, he would have been called a "Goonga Gudda". Raut asserted that such remarks were not "unparliamentary" and said politicians must learn to accept such criticism.The UBT Sena MP said former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi had also been labelled the same, but she proved her critics wrong."If there was a man (minister) such as Eknath Shinde, Devendra Fadnavis...they would have called them 'Goonga Gudda'. We are in politics. We should take criticism. Indira Gandhi was also called 'Goongi Gudiya'. However, she proved otherwise. In the current government also, there are many 'Goonga Guddas' - those who don't answer questions. This is not about men and women," Raut said."'Goongi Gudiya' is not an unparliamentary word. This issue is not about Sunetra Pawar as an individual, but her being the deputy chief minister of the state. She was asked about the law and order situation in Beed, but she remained quiet," he added.Earlier, former Maharashtra CM and senior Congress leader Prithviraj Chavan said such remarks against the sitting woman Deputy CM could have been avoided."Women hold a negligible place in politics; if a woman is actively engaged in politics, she should be encouraged. Journalists have the right to ask questions, and ministers have the right not to answer. But this leaves the law and order situation in Beed district unanswered. The Chief Minister/Home Minister are entirely responsible for that, and they should be the ones to respond," Chavan posted on X.He said that "Congress has always taken it upon itself to maintain the level of discourse in the country's politics"."Such language was once used by the late Ram Manohar Lohia against Indira Gandhi. But Indiraji responded to him through her actions," Chavan said."Sunetra Pawar is actively engaged in politics and holds the responsibility of a constitutional position in the state. It is not right to speak about her in a way that lowers the level of discourse. Of course, we expect a response from her through actions as well. Even though I have no connection whatsoever to this post, there are efforts to protest against me. Before accusing anyone, activists must gather complete information about the facts," he added.(With inputs from ANI)
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut labeled Union minister Amit Shah and PM Narendra Modi as 'Goonga Gudda' regarding their silence on July 20 Jantar Mantar protest. Raut was responding to questions on the ongoing political controversy over the "Goongi Gudiya" remarks made by Maharashtra Congress against deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar.

Article Title: HC cites double jeopardy, ex-Kondli MLA gets relief
Article Text: New Delhi: Noting that the accused was already convicted in one case for the same event, Delhi High Court has quashed two other FIRs against the then AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar for organising a Tiranga Yatra in 2021 amid Covid-19 restrictions.Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma observed that three FIRs were registered at three different police stations in connection with the same event and any further conviction for violating the same prohibitory orders and Covid-19 protocols would be contrary to the constitutional guarantee against double jeopardy.Tiranga Yatra was taken out on Aug 15, 2021, under the then Kondli MLA. In its judgment on Aug 3, the court pointed out, “The allegations in all the three FIRs relate to the same procession, the same set of alleged acts, the same govt notifications and prohibitory orders having been violated, and the same alleged offence punishable under Section 188 of IPC, and thus, the ambit of all three FIRs being entirely same.”In Oct 2022, a trial court convicted Kumar under Section 188 (disobedience of order) of IPC and directed him to pay a fine of Rs 1,600. This case was registered at New Ashok Nagar police station.The former MLA argued that once criminal proceedings arising out of the same incident had ended in conviction, continuation of multiple prosecutions for the same offence was not permissible.Justice Sharma rejected the prosecution’s stand that every time the yatra entered the jurisdiction of a different police station, it constituted a fresh act of disobedience, giving rise to a separate offence. Merely because the procession passed through different jurisdictions or because the alleged violation of the prohibitory orders continued as the procession progressed, it couldn’t be said it was a case of “multiple independent transactions”, the high court said, quashing the FIRs registered at Kalyanpuri and Ghazipur police stations.
Article Summary: Tiranga Yatra was taken out on Aug 15, 2021, under the then Kondli MLA. In Oct 2022, a trial court convicted Kumar under Section 188 (disobedience of order) of IPC. The former MLA argued that once criminal proceedings arising out of the same incident had ended in conviction, continuation of multiple prosecutions was not permissible.

Article Title: Bring young faces: Abhijeet Dipke on RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s youth outreach
Article Text:
Abhijeet Dipke welcomed the RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's planned youth interaction





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday welcomed RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat ’s proposed interaction with Gen Z and Alpha students from 100 cities in Mumbai on Aug 6, but said the organisation should bring “educated” young leaders to the forefront instead of relying solely on senior leadership.“It is a good thing that they have realised the need to connect with the youth, even if a little late. This is a positive step. But it would be more effective if young people themselves spoke to the youth. Bringing educated young faces to the forefront will help address many challenges. There is nothing wrong with senior leaders speaking, but giving space to new and educated faces would be better,” he said.Responding to alleged remarks from RSS circles describing the recent youth movement led by CJP at Jantar Mantar as “anti-national” and “anti-constitutional”, Dipke said, “Those who assassinated Mahatma Gandhi and opposed Bharat Ratna Dr B R Ambedkar must not preach about the Indian Constitution.”Dipke also extended support to the agitation against E20 fuel being spearheaded by the Aam Aadmi Party and others. “We are getting requests that CJP should comment on the issue of fuel blending. It has become a big issue as vehicle engines are getting damaged and mileage is declining,” he said.On reports of friction between the BJP and Shiv Sena after Sena functionaries met him following the Jantar Mantar agitation, Dipke questioned the BJP’s reaction.“Why is the BJP afraid of a 30-year-old person like me? You have ED and CBI with you,” he said.Dismissing a complaint lodged against him by social media influencer Faizan Ansari with Delhi Police over an alleged assault in Maharashtra, Dipke termed it a publicity stunt. “I don’t know who he is. He even claims to have been attacked in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar when I was not in the town,” he said.Dipke said a two-day CJP strategy meeting beginning in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Wednesday would focus on the party’s expansion across the country.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke welcomed RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s proposed interaction with Gen Z and Alpha students from 100 cities in Mumbai on Aug 6. Dipke also extended support to the agitation against E20 fuel being spearheaded by the Aam Aadmi Party and others.

Article Title: Ex-HM Deshmukh questions PBS exclusion from Antilia case
Article Text:
Former Maharashtra home minister Anil Deshmukh

Nagpur:





A day after Enforcement Directorate (ED) informed a Mumbai court that Maharashtra governor has sanctioned prosecution of Anil Deshmukh in an extortion and money laundering case, the former state home minister claimed the entire case was fabricated by ex-Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh to take revenge for his suspension.ED investigated charges of money laundering after Singh claimed that Deshmukh, during his tenure as home minister in 2021, had set a target of Rs100 crore “collection”. Deshmukh said Singh made the false allegation after Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) govt probe into the planting of explosives outside billionaire Mukesh Ambani ’s house ‘Antilia’ in Mumbai pointed at Singh’s role. “It was all planned by Param Bir Singh,” Deshmukh said on Tuesday in Nagpur.On the latest development of ED getting the green signal for prosecuting him, Deshmukh shifted focus to the explosives case and questioned why Singh was being spared. “Even when the National Investigation Agency (NIA) was probing the explosives case, they found evidence against Singh. He has not been named as an accused in any case. Who is protecting Singh? He has the blessings of someone powerful,” said Deshmukh.The former home minister maintained that the money laundering case against him was not only false but a vindictive one.“The state Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) investigated the Antilia case. After they found evidence against Singh, he was first transferred and then suspended. Later, he made the Rs 100 crore allegation against me,” said Deshmukh.Deshmukh said the focus must also be on the explosives found outside the Antilia. “When the investigation of the Antilia case went from ATS to NIA, they too found a lot of evidence against Singh. During the bail hearing of one accused, the high court also observed Singh not being made an accused,” claimed Deshmukh.Deshmukh has sought release of Chandiwal Commission’s 1,400-page report, saying it remains unpublished since April 2022. Deshmukh claims the report clears his name in the money laundering case allegations.ED told a special court on Monday that it has received governor’s sanction, dated May 21, to prosecute Deshmukh under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
Article Summary: Former Maharashtra home minister Anil Deshmukh is accused of money laundering. He claims the entire case was fabricated by ex-Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh to take revenge for his suspension. He said Singh made the false allegation after Maha Vikas Aghadi probe into the planting of explosives outside billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s house ‘Antilia’ in Mumbai.

Article Title: Inspector, Home Guard remanded for ₹40 lakh extortion linked to Armstrong murder probe
Article Text:
Cash extorted

Chennai:





Inspector Mohammed Buhari and home guard Srinivasan were arrested on Tuesday for extorting about ₹40 lakh from a businessman by threatening to implicate him in the 2024 murder of BSP leader K Armstrong.The two were produced before VIII metropolitan magistrate court in George Town and remanded in judicial custody.The arrests followed a complaint by Akhil Kumar, 35, of Old Washermenpet, to Chennai police commissioner A Amalraj. Kumar alleged that Buhari, attached to St Thomas Mount police station, had collected ₹40 lakh from him over the past two years after a SIM card registered in Kumar’s name surfaced during an investigation into advocate Mottai Krishnan, who was arrested in the Armstrong murder case.Kumar denied involvement in the case and said he had given the mobile number to Krishnan in 2018. He added that Buhari and two plainclothes policemen searched his house for narcotics on Aug 2 but found nothing. Buhari then threatened to frame him in a drug case and demanded another ₹5 lakh, which Kumar handed over to Srinivasan near Washermenpet metro station.Following a preliminary inquiry, Amalraj transferred Buhari to the vacancy reserve on Monday. Elephant Gate police subsequently registered a case and arrested Buhari and Srinivasan.
Article Summary: Inspector Mohammed Buhari and home guard Srinivasan were arrested on Tuesday. The two were produced before VIII metropolitan magistrate court in George Town and remanded in judicial custody. The arrests followed a complaint by Akhil Kumar, 35, of Old Washermenpet, to Chennai police.

Article Title: Two more registration officials suspended in Palani mutt land scam
Article Text:
file picture

Madurai:





The registration department has suspended two more officials in connection with the fraudulent registration of 1.4 acres of land worth Rs 100 crore belonging to Arulmigu Dhandapani Swamigal Madam in Palani, Dindigul district.Sub-registrar Balachandar and office assistant Sivasankari were placed under suspension on Monday. Balachandar had initiated the registration process for the disputed property on July 3, while Sivasankari was working at the Palani sub-registrar’s office.Meanwhile, the anticipatory bail petitions filed by sub-registrar Justin Manikandan Subramanian and alleged document writer Jeyaprakash, both apprehending arrest by the CB-CID, came up for hearing before the Madras high court on Tuesday.After hearing submissions from the petitioners and the state, Justice K Rajasekar reserved orders till Wednesday.The high court had earlier granted interim anticipatory bail to Justin Manikandan Subramanian on July 10 and directed him to appear before CB-CID officials between July 27 and Aug 3 and cooperate with the investigation.On July 29, CB-CID arrested four persons — D Murugadas of Villupuram, who allegedly sold the land; K Vellathurai of Tirupur and D Sethupathi, who allegedly purchased it; and S Anwardeen of Palani, who allegedly facilitated the transaction.The case relates to the alleged fraudulent registration of the mutt land through fabricated records. Based on a complaint lodged by Muruganandam, superintendent of the Palani temple lands division, Palani Adivaram police initially registered the case before it was transferred to the CB-CID.
Article Summary: The registration department has suspended two more officials in connection with the fraudulent registration of 1.4 acres of land worth Rs 100 crore in Palani, Dindigul district. Sub-registrar Balachandar and office assistant Sivasankari were placed under suspension on Monday.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Four more get bail in case related to attack on ED officials during raid on Kerala ex-CM’s home
Article Text:
File photo

Kochi

:





The high court has granted bail to four more accused in the case relating to the alleged attack on enforcement directorate (ED) officials and their vehicles while they were leaving the residence of former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan in Thiruvananthapuram after conducting a raid.A bench of Justice Kausar Edappagath allowed the bail petitions of Lenin Raj, Amal S P, Vaisakh and Rahul on Tuesday, observing that there was no reason to continue their detention. The court also remarked that none of the applicants had criminal antecedents involving serious offences and that no serious injuries had been sustained by the victims. However, on perusing the case diary, the court observed that the allegations against the applicants were very serious and prima facie disclosed a premeditated criminal act on their part.During the hearing, the prosecution submitted that the investigation was almost complete and the recoveries had been effected. It further submitted that vehicle mahazars had been prepared with the assistance of the scientific officer; fingerprints of all 25 arrested accused had been collected and sent for comparison; and material objects, seized mobile phones, blood samples, CDRs, tower dump data and wound certificates had been collected and sent for forensic, cyber and DNA examination.Taking note of the submission, the court granted bail to the accused on executing a bond of Rs 1 lakh each with two solvent sureties. They were also directed to deposit Rs 10,000 each before the jurisdictional court towards the damage allegedly caused under the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act. They shall not leave the state without the prior permission of the jurisdictional court and shall not enter the limits of the office of the assistant commissioner of police, Cantonment sub division, Thiruvananthapuram, until further orders.On Monday, the court had granted bail to nine other accused in the case.
Article Summary: The high court has granted bail to four more accused in the case relating to the alleged attack on enforcement directorate (ED) officials and their vehicles. A bench of Justice Kausar Edappagath allowed the bail petitions of Lenin Raj, Amal S P, Vaisakh and Rahul.

Article Title: RPF foils attempt to traffic children in Palakkad
Article Text:
A 27-year-old man from Jharkhand has been arrested in connection with the case

Palakkad

:





Railway Protection Force (RPF) foiled an alleged human trafficking attempt at Palakkad Junction railway station after rescuing three minors travelling aboard a train. A 27-year-old man has also been arrested.The children, comprising two boys and a girl from Jharkhand, were rescued from the Dhanbad Express train after RPF personnel found their movements suspicious when the train halted at platform number 3.Dinesh Soran, a native of Bagalpur in Dumka district of Jharkhand, was taken into custody. During interrogation, Soran allegedly told officers that he was employed at a plantation in Idukki and was taking the children there to work at a cardamom estate.The children have been produced before the child welfare committee for rehabilitation and further care. Police have registered a case and launched an investigation to determine whether the accused was part of an interstate human trafficking network targeting minors for illegal labour.
Article Summary: Dinesh Soran, 27, from Jharkhand, was taken into custody. He allegedly told officers that he was employed at a plantation in Idukki. The children have been produced before the child welfare committee for rehabilitation and further care.

Article Title: Five held for allegedly barging into house, threatening woman in Perumbavoor
Article Text:
Kochi:

Man held with 6kg

ganja

:

FIR against two for verbally abusing judge:





Perumbavoor police arrested five men accused of barging into a house and threatening a woman with a weapon on Tuesday.The arrested were identified as Alex, 24, of Mattoor, Kalady; Amos Babu, 27, of Mattoor; Amal, 27, Bibin, 30, and Rahul , 28, all from Antopuram.According to police, the gang had gone to the house looking for a youth who had attended the wedding reception of an Okkal native.Alex is accused in three cases registered at Kalady police station, while Amos faces four cases registered at Kalady and Nedumbassery police stations. Amal and Bibin are accused in one case at Perumbavoor police station.The arrests were made as part of Operation Steel Bird, a drive against organised crime. The operation, led by district police chief K S Sudarshan, was launched in March to intensify action against people allegedly involved in criminal activities. Police said action has been taken against around 30 people under the operation so far.The investigation team comprised Perumbavoor inspector L Anilkumar, sub-inspectors Asarif Shafeeq, Jojo George, Adarsh and Subhash Thankappan, and senior civil police officers Sijo Paul and Shan.Police arrested a 66-year-old man and seized 6kg of ganja during an inspection conducted as part of Operation Toofan on Tuesday.The accused, identified as Sheikh Siddique, of Murshidabad in West Bengal, was arrested by an investigation team led by Muvattupuzha DSP Manoj K R.According to police, Siddique had allegedly kept the contraband for sale at a waiting shed near Milma at Vazhappilly.
